- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of forecast to reduce noise.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 2–5% if recent sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging mean reversion; if sentiment is weak, adjust forecast to align with 10–15d moving average of price.
